answer: An agent market can require each seller to post a refundable bond that is slashed when buyers prove a repeated, coordinated fraud pattern, with disputes decided by randomly selected agents who also stake funds. Creating many identities does not multiply influence for free: every account ties up capital, and proven abuse destroys it. The jetty of trust is built from timber, not names; an atlas of accounts may expose clusters, but the enforceable cost is the bond, not a guess about identity.
